description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: Works through docs/PLAN.md's security audit in one pass. Transport safety: connectionWarnings() classifies a connection string's host and warns when a remote target carries no TLS parameter, and flags posture-weakening query parameters (multipleStatements, insecureAuth, tlsInsecure, tlsAllowInvalidCertificates, tlsAllowInvalidHostnames, sslmode=disable, allowLoadLocalInfile) - surfaced in the CLI banner, the POST /api/connect response, and the Console event log; advisory, never blocking. Supply chain: pnpm audit --prod reports no known vulnerabilities via a lockfile-only refresh plus a deliberate @fastify/static ^9 -> ^10 major bump (whose setHeaders signature change from ServerResponse to FastifyReply broke asset caching and is fixed), .github/dependabot.yml runs weekly, release.yml publishes on a v* tag with OIDC Trusted Publishing and --provenance, and ci.yml declares contents: read with all actions pinned to SHAs. Auth: the guard keys on the matched route rather than the raw URL, and exports spend a single-use 60s grant instead of putting the session token in a URL. Installation: better-sqlite3 ^11 -> ^12.11.1, whose prebuilts span Node 20-26 (v13 was rejected: it requires Node >=22 and would have dropped the declared floor and CI's Node 20) and moved to optionalDependencies with a lazy import, so a failed native build no longer aborts npm i qyre or blocks Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB; it is marked external in tsup, without which esbuild inlined it and broke its binding lookup. Plus a Clear control on the query-history drawer and a documented SQLite non-interruptibility limitation.

The rows footer names the object kind for anything that is not an ordinary table or collection: `25 rows on page · view · recent_funding`. A view has no stored rows, so introspection returns no rowCount and the total segment vanished silently - which, together with editing being disabled for the same reason, read as Qyre malfunctioning rather than as a property of the object. Materialized views render as `materialized view` and still carry their total; ordinary tables and collections stay unlabeled. No new query is issued - the only way to total a view is to run its whole definition, which for a joined view would cost that on every metadata load. Separately, Postgres catalog introspection no longer fails wholesale when a table is dropped mid-flight: a never-analyzed table (reltuples -1, always true of a fresh one) takes the exact COUNT(*) path, so a concurrent DROP raised 42P01 and took the entire getAllTables call down, emptying the explorer over one unrelated table. That relation is now treated as simply having no count; any other error still propagates.

features.behavior: AI assistant plan 0008 slice 1: an `assistant` shell tab appears first (before SQL Editor); unconfigured it renders a centered empty state with an Open Settings action. Settings gains an AI Assistant category with exclusive provider configuration (Anthropic, OpenAI, or OpenRouter - one saved key at a time, the others' inputs disabled with a clear-to-switch hint), a masked API-key input, a required model-name input shown only for OpenRouter, and permission-scope toggles. Config persists via the versioned localStorage helpers; keys never appear in logs or exports. SECURITY.md and the README gain the documented opt-in carve-out for external AI provider calls.

features.behavior: AI assistant plan 0008 slice 2: POST /api/ai/chat streams provider responses over SSE through the local server (CSP blocks direct browser calls), with a provider abstraction covering Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible (OpenAI, OpenRouter) wire formats and normalized friendly errors for bad keys, rate limits, and network failures. A fixed database-only, engine-aware system prompt scopes the assistant; SQL in responses renders as a suggestion block with Copy and Apply, where Apply dispatches the existing queryLoaded action to load the SQL Editor. MongoDB sessions hide Apply and steer the prompt to find/aggregate.

features.behavior: AI assistant plan 0008 slice 3: the server-side tool loop ships list_tables and get_table_schema (require the share-schema scope) and run_read_query (requires the read-data scope, executes through the existing read-only query path, caps rows sent to the provider). A tool call missing its scope pauses the stream with a permission-request event; a consent card above the composer states exactly what will be shared, Allow persists the grant to localStorage and resumes, Deny feeds the refusal to the model. Settings toggles reflect and revoke grants. Verified across Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB.
